brief: Santander's Stephen Stanley adds a 25bp March 2027 hike to his Fed call (previously September and December 2026 hikes then a hold through 2027), making three quarter-point hikes in six months. Four developments drive the change. First, Q3 GDP showed 5.0% annualized real domestic demand and a 165K October payroll gain with wages accelerating, pushing Fed officials from "full employment box checked, focus on inflation" toward fear of overheating. Second, inflation is broadening: shelter costs (rent/OER, Zillow) are reaccelerating, core services ex-housing PCE hit 3.6% y/y, and officials now cite AI-buildout demand rather than just tariffs/energy. Third, officials across the hawk-dove spectrum now judge the neutral rate higher than assumed, meaning current policy is less restrictive than thought. Fourth, anecdotal and survey evidence (NFIB Price Plans, Fed officials) suggests businesses are finally passing through input costs. Stanley still expects a cautious every-other-meeting pace (January skip, March hike, possible June hike if overheating persists) rather than back-to-back moves, and bets inflation relief arrives by spring.

cards.claim: Santander's Stephen Stanley adds a 25 basis point Fed rate hike in March 2027 to his existing call, on top of hikes in September and December 2026, totaling three quarter-point increases over roughly six months.
cards.anchor: I am adding another tightening move in March 2027.

cards.claim: Stanley had previously projected a 25bp December 2026 hike followed by the Fed on hold through all of 2027.
cards.anchor: I have been projecting that the FOMC would hike by 25 basis points in December and then be on hold for all of 2027.

cards.claim: Real consumer spending rose at a 3.8% annualized rate in Q3, matching the prior quarter's pace.
cards.anchor: Real consumer spending posted a stellar 3.8% annualized gain for a second straight quarter

cards.claim: Business fixed investment grew by more than 13% annualized in Q3, the best quarter in 15 years outside the 2020 post-COVID rebound.
cards.anchor: business fixed investment surged in real terms by over 13% annualized, the best quarter in 15 years

cards.claim: Real domestic demand grew at a 5.0% annualized pace in Q3, the best performance since the 2020-21 COVID bounce.
cards.anchor: real domestic demand increased at a 5.0% annualized pace in Q3, the best performance since the 2020-21 COVID bounce

cards.claim: October payrolls rose by 165K, the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, and average hourly earnings accelerated to a 0.4% monthly gain.
cards.anchor: Payrolls posted a 165K gain, the unemployment rate inched down to 4.1%, and average hourly earnings accelerated to a 0.4% rise

cards.claim: Initial jobless claims have held at or below 200K every week since early September.
cards.anchor: initial jobless claims have taken another leg down in recent months, holding at or below 200K every week since early September

cards.claim: New York Fed President Williams said the US economy continues to grow and seems to be strengthening.
cards.anchor: the US economy not only continues to grow but actually seems to be strengthening

cards.claim: Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said AI data center buildout demand is adding old-fashioned overheating that appears to be spreading beyond its own sector.
cards.anchor: we’re adding this old-fashioned demand overheating coming from the AI data center buildout, that looks like it’s starting to spread out of its lane.

cards.claim: Rent and owners' equivalent rent have posted annualized increases of 3.4% and 3.8% respectively over the past seven months since April.
cards.anchor: rent and OER posting annualized increases of 3.4% and 3.8%, respectively, over the last seven months.

cards.claim: The Zillow Rent Index has risen by 0.3% or more per month in each of the past five months, up from 0.1-0.2% previously.
cards.anchor: The Zillow Rent Index has increased by 0.3% or more in each of the past five months

cards.claim: The core services ex housing component of the PCE deflator rose 0.5% in August and 0.4% in September.
cards.anchor: The core services ex housing component of the PCE deflator rose by 0.5% in August and 0.4% in September.

cards.claim: The year-over-year rate for core services ex housing PCE inflation reached 3.6% in September, the highest since late 2024.
cards.anchor: has moved up this year, reaching 3.6% in September, the highest reading since late 2024.

cards.claim: The Cleveland Fed's Median CPI measure rose to +0.3% in October.
cards.anchor: The Median CPI picked up to +0.3% in October

cards.claim: The Cleveland Fed's 16% Trimmed-Mean CPI measure rose to +0.4% in October from +0.3% in September, with its year-over-year rate accelerating by three tenths over two months to 2.9%.
cards.anchor: in September to +0.4% in October, with the year-over-year advance accelerating by a combined three tenths over the past two months to 2.9%.

cards.claim: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said the most recent data show inflation moving in the wrong direction.
cards.anchor: the most recent data that I’ve seen show inflation is moving in the wrong direction.

cards.claim: Kansas City Fed President Schmid said he did not think the fed funds rate was restrictive last year and now believes it is fairly accommodative.
cards.anchor: I didn’t think our rate was restrictive last year, and I believe today it’s fairly accommodative.

cards.claim: Dallas Fed President Logan estimated the fed funds target range is at least 50 basis points below the level that would create modest restriction.
cards.anchor: the fed funds target range is at least 50 basis points – half a percentage point – below the level that would create some modest restriction

cards.claim: Richmond Fed President Barkin said he views policy as currently close to neutral, though vigorous consumer spending could make the case that it is a bit accommodative.
cards.anchor: views policy as currently close to neutral, though he could make a case, based on vigorous consumer spending, that it may be a bit accommodative.

cards.claim: New York Fed President Williams and San Francisco Fed President Daly, both considered dovish-leaning, called over the past week for additional rate hiking.
cards.anchor: New York Fed President Williams and San Francisco Fed President Daly, called over the past week for additional rate hiking.

cards.claim: Stanley's prior Fed call assumed the FOMC was raising its neutral rate estimate by about 50 basis points to around 3.5%.
cards.anchor: the FOMC was nudging up the range of estimates of neutrality by around 50 basis points to center close to 3½%.

cards.claim: Fed Governor Waller raised the possibility of a 50 basis point rate hike in December.
cards.anchor: Governor Waller on Tuesday raised the possibility of a 50 basis point rate hike in December

cards.claim: Fed Governor Waller cited a Fed Board staff paper finding that ISM survey commodity price data predicts PPI a few months later and eventually PCE deflators.
cards.anchor: the list of commodities reported up and down in price in ISM surveys has predictive value for the PPI a few months later

cards.claim: Fed Governor Waller said the October ISM data point to the possibility of more price increases ahead.
cards.anchor: the October ISM data “point to the possibility of more price increases ahead.”

cards.claim: Richmond Fed President Barkin said many businesses feel their margins are squeezed and are weighing whether they can pass costs on to prices.
cards.anchor: I’ve talked to a lot of businesses who do feel their margins are squeezed

cards.claim: San Francisco Fed President Daly said more producers are saying they want to pass on costs.
cards.anchor: more producers are saying that they want to pass on costs.

cards.claim: The NFIB Small Business Survey's Price Plans index jumped six points to +37 in October, the highest since 2022.
cards.anchor: the “Price Plans” gauge jumped by six points to +37

cards.claim: The IEA said oil supply outpaced demand in October for the first time since the conflict began.
cards.anchor: for the first time since the conflict began, oil supply outpaced demand in October

cards.claim: Stanley expects the FOMC to skip tightening in January 2027 and then hike in March if needed, following the same skip-then-hike pattern as September-December 2026.
cards.anchor: a January skip and, if necessary, a hike in March.

cards.claim: Stanley said a fourth rate hike in June 2027 is possible if the economy keeps overheating or core inflation stays at or above 3% into next year.
cards.anchor: we could see a fourth rate increase in June.

cards.claim: The September FOMC dot plot projected a median 2027 year-end rate of 4.125%, with the highest estimates at 4.375%.
cards.anchor: The September FOMC dot projections for 2027, with the median at 4.125% and the highest estimates at 4.375%

cards.claim: A cumulative 75 basis points of hikes from September 2026 through March 2027 would fully unwind the rate cuts implemented in 2025.
cards.anchor: a cumulative 75 basis points of rate increases would unwind the easing implemented in 2025

cards.claim: Stanley's own bet is that the Fed will get some relief on inflation data by spring 2027.
cards.anchor: My current bet is that some degree of relief will arrive by the spring.
